script: Spread and total were not saved for CIN@PIT, so this script is inferred only from weeks 1-2 form. Cincinnati has a bell-cow in C.Brown (36 carries, 136 rush yards) and an outside volume receiver in T.Higgins (16 targets, 154 yards, 210 air yards), while Pittsburgh's downfield game is empty: D.Metcalf has 19 targets and 266 air yards but only 67 receiving yards, and A.Rodgers is negative EPA both vs blitz (-0.36, n=23) and without (-0.42). Cincinnati should move it on the ground against a Pittsburgh front allowing 4.54 YPC and 7 runs of 10+, and through T.Higgins outside where Pittsburgh allows 9.1 YPA left (20 att) and 8.53 right (17 att). Pittsburgh is stuck in a committee grind — J.Warren 21 carries for 89 yards, R.Dowdle 15 for 37 — because Cincinnati blitzes only 11% and A.Rodgers has been worse in the non-blitz looks he will mostly see.
who_goes_off: T.Higgins is the one who should go off: 154 receiving yards on 16 targets and 210 air yards over weeks 1-2 (77.0 per game) into a Pittsburgh perimeter that has already allowed 7 pass plays of 20+ on 51 attempts. C.Brown is the rush piece who can also pop — 18 carries and 68.0 rush yards per game — because Pittsburgh's 4.54 YPC and 7 runs of 10+ is a softer front than the 3.78 YPC he has posted on 36 carries. J.Warren should not go off as a rusher: 89 yards on 21 carries (44.5 per game) with R.Dowdle taking 15 carries, against a Cincinnati defense at 4.05 YPC and only 4 runs of 10+.
weak_spot: Pittsburgh's real weak spot is the outside and the run front, not the middle: left 9.1 YPA on 20 attempts, right 8.53 on 17, middle only 3.43 on a tiny 7 attempts, plus 4.54 rush YPC and 7 runs of 10+. That is an outside-receiver and lead-back matchup (T.Higgins, C.Brown), not a middle-of-field LBs/nickel/safeties attack. Cincinnati's hole is the middle at 8.89 YPA on 18 attempts and the left at 8.04 on 28, while the right is sound at 5.11 YPA on 36 attempts and the run front has allowed only 4 runs of 10+ at 4.05 YPC.
injury_fallout: No injury report was saved for CIN@PIT, so there is no injury fallout to price and weeks 1-2 usage stands as the role chart: C.Brown 36 carries to S.Perine's 7, T.Higgins 16 targets to J.Chase's 13 and 87 yards, J.Warren 21 carries to R.Dowdle's 15, and D.Metcalf 19 targets for only 67 yards.
qb_vs_blitz: J.Burrow is -0.62 EPA/dropback vs blitz (n=24) and +0.27 with no blitz, and Pittsburgh blitzes only 25%, so most of his dropbacks should land in the profitable non-blitz bucket that feeds T.Higgins' 210 air yards rather than a pressure script. A.Rodgers is -0.36 EPA vs blitz (n=23) and -0.42 with no blitz, and Cincinnati blitzes just 11%, so he is likely stuck in the worse non-blitz sample — the same environment in which D.Metcalf's 266 air yards became only 67 receiving yards.

picks.why: T.Higgins is at 154 yards on 16 targets and 210 air yards across weeks 1-2, 77.0 per game against a 54.5 line, and Pittsburgh has allowed 9.1 YPA left and 8.53 right plus 7 gains of 20+ on 51 attempts. J.Burrow's +0.27 EPA with no blitz and Pittsburgh's 25% blitz rate say the clean-pocket script that produced those 16 targets should be the majority of Cincinnati dropbacks.

J.Warren has 89 rush yards on 21 carries over weeks 1-2 (44.5 per game) with R.Dowdle taking 15 carries for 37 yards, so a 58.0 rush line is volume he is not earning. Cincinnati allows 4.05 YPC and only 4 runs of 10+, and A.Rodgers' -0.42 EPA without blitz plus an 11% Cincinnati blitz rate does not project a trailing-script carry spike big enough to close a 13.5-yard gap.
